div.p: These rules bind the whole field force, which is why they live with the administrator and not with the manager they constrain.

sheet.div: People forget. At the end of the day anyone still on duty is signed out, and visits and trips that only lack the final tap are closed. A visit with no outcome, or a trip with no closing odometer, is left open on purpose — closing those would mean writing down an outcome nobody gave or a distance nobody drove. The hour is read in each executive's own timezone.

With attendance required, an executive cannot check in at a clinic or start their travel until they have started their day on My Day. It is marked on Odoo's own attendance record, so payroll and HR reporting see it without anything being copied across.
A check-in outside the radius is recorded and must be explained before the visit can be closed — never refused. Blocking it would only mean the visit goes unrecorded, which is worse.
These bands drive the Clinic Coverage report, the Marketing Desk's rescue list and the suggestions offered on My Day. Saving them rebuilds the report immediately.

When an executive registers a case, the same patient at the same clinic within this many days is flagged. The slip cannot become an order until they confirm it is genuinely a different case — never silently dropped and never silently duplicated, because the person at the counter is the only one who can tell which it is.
A rate set here is policy. An executive sees what they are paid per kilometre on their trip but cannot change it.

Cash an executive takes at a clinic goes into a petty cash float in their name at check-out, and comes off it when they hand the envelope to the office and the office counts it against the handover code. The float is a custody record — it never touches the ledger; accounts still books the receipt against the doctor's account. Cash held longer, or more, than these limits is chased on My Day and the Ops Desk.

Each executive's day assembles itself into a sheet at day close and crosses two desks in order — the Operational Manager vouches the day happened as recorded, then the Marketing Manager judges the activities. A sheet that outstays the SLA on either desk is raised with the administrators, once.
